title: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance

scenes.narration: Why does your phone charger get warm while fast-charging, or a ceiling fan slow down when voltage drops during summer in Bengaluru?
Think of an overhead water tank on your house roof. Water height is Voltage, water flow through the pipe is Current, and a narrow tap is Resistance.
Georg Ohm discovered that Voltage equals Current multiplied by Resistance: V equals I times R. Doubling voltage doubles the current if resistance stays constant.
Let's test a two hundred thirty volt Indian wall socket powering an iron box with forty-six ohms resistance. Two hundred thirty divided by forty-six gives five amperes of current.
To recap: Voltage pushes electrons, Resistance opposes them, and Current is the resulting flow governed by V equals I times R.

steps: Resistance (R): Opposition to flow in Ohms (Ω)
Current (I = V / R): Flow rate in Amperes
